# University of Jordan Summary
The University of Jordan (UJ), established by royal decree in 1962, is the first and largest university in Jordan. Its main campus is located in Jubaiha, north of Amman, covering 1,200 dunums (about 1.20 km²) and situated along University Street, a major thoroughfare with many amenities and student housing. A secondary campus was founded in Aqaba in 2009 to support regional development, featuring modern academic facilities and recreational areas.
Academic offerings at UJ encompass 78 undergraduate and 143 postgraduate programs across three streams: scientific faculties (including Science, Agriculture, Engineering—which is ABET-accredited—and Information Technology), humanitarian faculties (Arts, Sharia, Business, Law, Education, and others), and medical faculties (Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Dentistry, and Rehabilitation Sciences). The university operates the Jordan University Library with over one million items and multiple research centers, supporting significant scientific collections and publishing several peer-reviewed journals.
UJ is home to Jordan University Hospital, a leading teaching and research hospital in the region with advanced medical services and international accreditations. The university maintains numerous bilateral and international affiliations, enhancing student exchange and academic cooperation, and holds top national admission scores and rankings among Arab universities. Its alumni have been influential in politics, science, culture, and public service, including multiple former prime ministers and high-ranking officials.
